newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded in lower trade and analysts said they could rise again on Tuesday after strong buying after price fixing and rises in continuous trade, but were uncertain over the market's trend later.
Some analysts said market sentiment could be cooled if a Monday press report that Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko might quit the job, proved true.

"Despite the (Kolodko) report the market rose today, so it was probably taken only as a rumour, but if it really happens it might...cool down the market", said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
The main market's WIG index rose 2.5 percent to 16,510.9 and turnover fell to 143.2 million zlotys on both markets as 71 issues rose, eight fell and seven were flat.
Some analysts also said last week's central bank decision increasing mandatory reserves for banks was dimming the outlook for the market's heavyweights -- banks.
But some believed the bourse looked attractive despite its average 15.9 P/E ratio, and said it could go higher than January 27's record of 16,910.4 possibly this week or next.
Kety surged 10 percent in a moderate turnover, possibly reacting to last week's six-percent fall.
Kable rose 9.7 percent on news that Denmark's NKT Cables plans to increase its stake in the firm to over 50 percent.
Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA soared 65.5 percent to 48 zlotys in heavy trade on its bourse debut but analysts saw it flat or falling in profit-taking in the next few sessions.

Continuous trade amounted to 13.8 million zlotys with nine stocks up, five down and six flat. The WIG-20 index calculated during continuous trade closed 0.7 percent higher than at the regular session at 1,689.1.
